lines.text: Researchers took over five US Treasury web addresses for about three dollars each.
DNS is the internet's phone book. A record points a website name to a numbered address.
lines.title: What is DNS?

lines.text: If a company drops a rented address but forgets the record, the name still points there.
lines.title: The forgotten record

lines.text: The researchers rented addresses from AWS, checked them against a list of names, and released misses.
lines.title: The loop

lines.text: In 48 hours they went through 450,000 addresses and took over 28 live ones.
lines.title: 48 hours

lines.text: Five were treasury.gov subdomains. A real .gov name makes a phishing page look trustworthy.
lines.title: Real targets

lines.text: AWS banned the account, but the addresses moved to a new account. AWS said it plans no change.
lines.title: The ban

lines.text: Delete DNS records the moment you stop using an address.
lines.title: Takeaway
